claims.text: Laser Powder Bed Fusion followed by rapid thermal annealing can fabricate the proposed Group IV–V refractory high-entropy alloy family.
LPBF followed by rapid thermal annealing will produce a nanostructured microstructure.
LPBF followed by rapid thermal annealing will produce a single-phase BCC microstructure.
The LPBF-plus-annealing route will mitigate embrittlement caused by interstitial impurities.
The LPBF-plus-annealing route will enhance high-temperature ductility relative to conventional casting.
Powder-metallurgy feedstocks for these alloys inherently contain oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon interstitial impurities.
High-energy-density LPBF induces rapid solidification and in-situ alloy formation.
Rapid thermal solution annealing will homogenize the additively manufactured microstructure.
Rapid thermal annealing will refine grain size and relieve residual stresses.
Processing under argon will minimize additional interstitial uptake.
Annealing between 1000°C and 1400°C is sufficient to homogenize the proposed alloys without melting them.
Controlled cooling after annealing will prevent precipitation of brittle topologically close-packed phases.
The optimized microstructure will have suppressed elemental segregation and reduced interstitial clustering.
High configurational entropy stabilizes disordered solid solutions relative to ordered intermetallic phases.
Interstitial impurities cause lattice distortion and elastic instability responsible for intrinsic brittleness.
Annealing mitigates interstitial brittleness by producing a more uniform distribution of solutes and interstitials.
Alloying intrinsically brittle Mo and W with subgroup IV or V transition metals can induce a brittle-to-ductile transition through electronic-structure changes and Jahn–Teller distortions.
The processed alloy will exhibit more than 10% room-temperature plastic strain.
The processed alloy will retain more than 400 MPa yield strength at 1600°C.

Conventionally cast versions of the same alloys typically have coarse grains, microsegregation, brittle intermetallic phases, and less than 1% room-temperature plastic strain because of interstitial embrittlement.

contradictions.description: The target is defined as a Group IV–V alloy family based on Ti/Zr/Hf and V/Nb/Ta, but the boundary example Nb–Mo–Ta–W–V and the proposed Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 test alloy contain Group VI Mo and W and contain no Group IV element.
